content: {"summary":"PAYAPI‑E1107 began at 09:05 UTC after the new card‑processor‑proxy release and was undone by executing a Kubernetes rollout undo, which restored the previous proxy version and caused the error to stop.","likely_cause":"Bug introduced in the freshly shipped card‑processor‑proxy build caused payments‑api to emit PAYAPI‑E1107 errors.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Errors started at 09:05 after the new proxy version was deployed","evidence_ids":["INC-0096#0"],"quote":"From 09:05, payments that went through the new version of the proxy failed, and payments-api logged `PAYAPI-E1107`"},{"text":"Operator ran a rollback command at 09:10","evidence_ids":["INC-0096#0"],"quote":"At 09:10 I ran `kubectl -n payments rollout undo deploy/card-processor-proxy`"},{"text":"After the rollback, PAYAPI‑E1107 stopped emitting","evidence_ids":["INC-0096#1"],"quote":"`PAYAPI-E1107` tailed off and then stopped"}],"next_checks":["Identify the specific code change in the 5 Nov 2025 release that broke processor calls","Add a pre‑ready health check that validates processor connectivity before marking pods ready","Review rollout policy to include a pause after the first pod update","Document the rollback procedure in the release checklist"]}
